questions.skill: Decide whether a model is consistent with observed results using a simulation
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A coin is claimed to be fair. It landed heads 34 times in 50 flips. The histogram shows 200 simulated runs of 50 fair flips. Is the claim consistent with the result? Justify with the simulation.
questions.prompt_markup: A coin is claimed to be fair. It landed heads 34 times in 50 flips. The histogram shows 200 simulated runs of 50 fair flips. Is the claim consistent with the result? Justify with the simulation.
questions.correct_answer: No: only 3 of 200 runs (1.5%) had 34 or more heads, so 34 heads is very unusual for a fair coin
questions.grading_note: Form required: decision and the simulated proportion.

questions.skill: Design a simulation to test a model
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Describe a simulation to test whether a basketball player really makes 70% of free throws, given that she made 11 of 20.
questions.prompt_markup: Describe a simulation to test whether a basketball player really makes 70% of free throws, given that she made 11 of 20.
questions.correct_answer: Use random digits 0-9 with 0-6 = make; take 20 digits per run, count makes; repeat many runs; see how often 11 or fewer makes occur.
questions.grading_note: Any valid design with all parts.

sections.skill: Compare two treatments with a re-randomization simulation

branch.new_demand: Apply the same model-testing logic to a randomized experiment.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the designed simulation for one proportion becomes a shuffle of treatment labels.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Compare two treatments with a re-randomization simulation
questions.standard_level: Algebra II. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra II, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: In an experiment, fertilized plants grew 2.9 cm more on average. In 200 re-randomizations, none of the differences was 2.9 cm or more. What do you conclude?
questions.prompt_markup: In an experiment, fertilized plants grew 2.9 cm more on average. In 200 re-randomizations, none of the differences was 2.9 cm or more. What do you conclude?
questions.correct_answer: The difference is very unlikely by chance alone, so the fertilizer appears to increase growth
